title: The canonical relative multiplicative group on the punctured affine line
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. The relative multiplicative group $\mathbf G_{m,S}$ is the existing punctured affine line $D(t)\subset\mathbf A^1_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space], with projection to $S$. Its multiplication, identity and inverse are the group-scheme operations [def-sc-group-scheme] locally given by $t\mapsto t\otimes t$, $t\mapsto1$ and $t\mapsto t^{-1}$. Equivalently put $R=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, let $R[t,t^{-1}]$ be finite formal Laurent sums with coefficients in $R$, with convolution multiplication, and pull the Laurent Hopf spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] back along the canonical map $S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ using fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a unique isomorphism of this model with $D(t)$ over $S$ pulling the existing unit coordinate back to the Laurent coordinate. Transporting the displayed Hopf group law through that uniquely specified isomorphism equips the existing punctured line with its canonical group law. For a generalized point $a:T\to\mathbf G_{m,S}$, its scalar is the pullback of this unit coordinate in $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. No field or nonempty-base assumption is imposed.
